close_reason: Fixed. Dropped the `let obj_json = &obj_val;` rebinding; the four `.get(...)` calls now invoke `obj_val.get(...)` directly. cargo fmt + clippy -p jmap-calendars-server -- -D warnings + cargo test -p jmap-calendars-server + RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p jmap-calendars-server --no-deps all clean. Committed 48fff94.
description:
event.rs:215:
    let obj_json = &obj_val;
    let has_utc_start = obj_json
        .get("utcStart")
        ...

The rebinding does nothing useful — obj_json is just a second name for &obj_val, and the subsequent .get() calls would compile identically against obj_val directly because serde_json::Value::get takes &self and Rust auto-borrows for method calls. The rebinding is also asymmetric with the update branch (event.rs:312-331), which calls patch_val.get(...) directly without an intermediate &alias.

Either delete line 215 and use obj_val.get("utcStart") on lines 216-228, or wait — actually obj_val is moved into the 'Value::Object(mut m) => …' arm at line 259. So the rebinding could be defensible if there's a borrow-vs-move issue.

Re-reading: line 215 binds &obj_val for the validation block (215-243). Line 258 takes obj_val by value in the next match. So the borrow IS the right shape — but the rebinding adds no signal. Calling obj_val.get(...) directly auto-borrows for the duration of each method call without needing the named &alias.

The fix is one line: delete line 215, replace 'obj_json' with 'obj_val' on lines 217-227. Reduces noise without changing semantics.
title: Useless rebinding 'let obj_json = &obj_val;' in CalendarEvent/set create path
